learning_objectives.statement: Show that multiplying two unit fractions finds a part of a part and can make a quantity smaller.
Compare a product of unit fractions with one of the factors.

prerequisites.statement: Name a unit fraction as one equal part of a whole.

misconception_catalog.statement: The learner treats multiplication as always making a quantity larger, including when both factors are less than 1.

artefacts.source_title: LessonCraft synthetic: a part of a part
artefacts.attribution: Original LessonCraft synthetic lesson for product validation. Not official Cameroon curriculum.
artefacts.page_or_section: Section A — Taking a part of a part
artefacts.body: A whole bar can be split into two equal parts. Each part is 1/2. If you take 1/2 of that 1/2, you keep one of two halves of a half. That piece is 1/4 of the original bar. Multiplying 1/2 × 1/2 means taking a part of a part. Because each factor is less than 1, the product 1/4 is smaller than 1/2, not larger. Adding 1/2 + 1/2 would make 1; multiplying does not.

flowchart LR
  whole["Whole bar"] --> half["1/2 of the bar"]
  half --> quarter["1/2 of that half = 1/4"]
  quarter --> smaller["1/4 is smaller than 1/2"]

reteach_visual_spec.mermaid:
flowchart TB
  bar["Four equal squares in one bar"] --> shade["Shade two squares: 1/2"]
  shade --> halfOfHalf["Keep one of those two: 1/4"]
  halfOfHalf --> compare["1/4 sits below 1/2 on the bar"]

diagnostic.prompt: Someone says: “1/2 × 1/2 is 1, because multiplying makes numbers bigger.” What is 1/2 × 1/2, and is that product larger or smaller than 1/2?

check.prompt: Is 1/3 × 1/2 larger or smaller than 1/3? What is the product?

reteach_check.prompt: Shade a story: you eat half of half a loaf. What fraction of the loaf is that, and is it more or less than half a loaf?
